_source: Ekkaa Electronics (India) Limited DRHP dated 24-Sep-2026 (SEBI filing 01-Oct-2026). Rs crore = Rs million / 10. Printed page = PDF page - 5. FY26 is consolidated (subsidiary Ekkaa Electronics Industries Pvt Ltd acquired 29-Aug-2025); FY24 and FY25 are standalone and not like-for-like (proforma on pp. 375-388). FY24 revenue is nominal: manufacturing began in 2024.

basis.name: Ekkaa Electronics (India) Limited
basis.brlm: Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors Limited; Shannon Advisors Private Limited (marketing only)
basis.outside: none for the issuer (all figures from the DRHP); merchant-banker section uses secondary sources marked unverified

1.finding: Bonus (1:1 on 28-Aug-2025, 3:1 on 20-Aug-2026) and the 1:2 split are applied to every period: FY26 EPS 9.04 on about 72.3 m weighted shares, FY25 EPS 3.63, FY24 EPS (0.62), all on the post-bonus count. Basic EPS already counts the compulsorily convertible preference shares, so basic and diluted EPS are equal.

2.finding: Operating cash flow was negative in all three years: -286.59 / -641.12 / -152.83 (Rs m, FY26/25/24) against PAT 653.79 / 235.52 / -40.50. Cumulative CFO is -1,080.54 m against cumulative PAT of 848.81 m. Receivables and inventory absorbed Rs 972.55 m and Rs 388.97 m in FY26 alone; capex of Rs 893.28 m was funded by debt and preference capital.

3.finding: Current tax Rs 145.42 m on PBT Rs 796.30 m (18.3%) in FY26; cumulative current tax 15.6% of cumulative PBT (Rs 163.74 m / Rs 1,048.80 m). The statutory rate applied is 17.16% (concessional manufacturing regime). Cash taxes paid were Rs 59.60 m over three years against Rs 163.74 m current tax charged, with Rs 131.71 m of current tax liability unpaid at 31-Mar-2026.

4.finding: Subsidiary Ekkaa Electronics Industries was owned by promoter-directors until 29-Aug-2025 and was the issuer's largest customer in FY25 (Rs 1,043.40 m, 21.01% of revenue) and a large supplier (Rs 894.49 m purchases); the issuer borrowed Rs 1,708.58 m from it in FY25. Acquisition price Rs 490.00 m (Rs 397.58 m in shares at Rs 888 and Rs 92.42 m cash), paid to the two promoter-directors. FY26 revenue still includes Rs 758.07 m (6.20%) of sales to it before acquisition. Rent and an advance to promoter-linked entities (Gaurisuta) in FY26.

5.finding: Fresh issue is amount-based (Rs 5,250 m), so there is no fixed share count and no objects price floor. Rs 2,250 m repays debt and Rs 1,500 m funds working capital; the rest is offer expenses and general corporate purposes (cap 25% of gross proceeds).

6.finding: Revaluation reserve not separately located in this pass.

7.finding: The restated accounts record the Rs 490 m acquisition as a bargain purchase: customer-relationship intangible Rs 37.08 m and capital reserve Rs 20.39 m, no goodwill. The proforma balance sheet shows goodwill of Rs 84.99 m for the same transaction: the two documents carry different purchase accounting. The seller was a related party of the issuer.

8.finding: Demand: LED televisions 71.78% of FY26 revenue; top customer 16.86%, top-5 52.43%, top-10 65.77% (FY25: 21.01%, 70.05%, 80.35%); customers unnamed. Supply: top supplier 46.94%, top-5 69.74%, top-10 79.11% of FY26 raw-material purchases; imported open cells and PCB parts. Geographic split not disclosed.

9.finding: No contingent liability requiring disclosure at 31-Mar-2026. Capital commitments not reviewed.

R1.finding: FY24 and FY25 restated figures derive from special-purpose Ind AS statements prepared for the offer (previous GAAP statutory accounts; transition date 01-Apr-2024). Statutory auditor M S K A & Associates LLP. Backup log of the accounting software kept only from 18-Feb-2026; audit-trail feature stated as enabled throughout FY26.

R5.finding: Offer is made under Reg 6(2) (at least 75% to QIBs) because the issuer does not satisfy Reg 6(1)(b): operating profit was negative (Rs -11.96 m) in FY24. Average operating profit over three years Rs 487.76 m; net tangible assets Rs 2,532.49 m; monetary assets 0.92% of net tangible assets.

R6.finding: BRLMs Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors (14 IPOs in FY2026-27) and Shannon Advisors (marketing role only; two IPOs listed since FY2025-26, one at a 37% day-30 discount). Fuller track record not compiled.

rationale.g1: FY26 revenue Rs 12,217.63 m is +72.3% on proforma FY25 Rs 7,093.37 m and proforma FY25 was +63.6% on FY24 (p. 137). Installed capacity 5.2 m units at 37.80% utilisation (p. 247). Issuer-commissioned Frost & Sullivan puts consumer appliances at 13.7% CAGR FY26-30 and LED TVs at 12.9% (pp. 168, 171). Bear = industry-rate growth; Bull = about half the proforma pace.
rationale.m: EBITDA margin 2.68% / 9.21% / 9.36% proforma FY24 / FY25 / FY26 (p. 137); gross margin flat at 17.0-17.6%, so margin gain came from operating leverage and fixed-cost absorption. Bear = midway between FY24 and FY26; Bull = FY26 level.
rationale.nwc: Trade NWC (inventory + receivables - payables) 7.5% of proforma FY25 revenue and 22.4% of FY26 revenue (pp. 73, 380); issuer's own net working-capital days 23 in FY26 (p. 137). Neutral holds the FY26 level; Bull assumes a return towards the FY25 level as supplier credit rebuilds; Bear assumes a further build.
rationale.roic: RoCE 18.00% FY26, 18.67% proforma (p. 137). Terminal ROIC is set above the c.16.6% WACC in every case; Bear is close to WACC.
